findings.who: A shareholder whose 2025 K-1 shows only income and no distribution, but who carries a loss suspended in 2024 for lack of basis. This year's income gives them enough basis to deduct it.
findings.why_no: The computed gate looks only at this year's K-1 loss or deduction items and box 16 code D. A loss carried from an earlier year is not on the 2025 K-1, so the gate is false.
findings.line: f7203.line1_if_req (and f7203.line2_if_req, f7203.election_if_req; the carryover in Part III column (b) is never reached)
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Are claiming a deduction for their share of an aggregate loss from an S corporation (including an aggregate loss not allowed last year because of basis limitations)"; p. 4, Column (b): "Enter any loss or deduction items disallowed due to basis limitations in prior years that were carried forward."
findings.fix: Broaden the gate with an input: "For this S corporation, do you have losses or deductions from earlier years that you could not deduct because your basis was too low (for example, column (e) of your 2024 Form 7203)?" A yes makes Form 7203 required.

findings.who: A shareholder who sold, redeemed, gifted, or otherwise disposed of some or all of the S corporation stock in 2025. Their K-1 shows income and no distribution.
findings.why_no: The gate tests only for loss or deduction items and non-dividend distributions. A disposition is not either, so the gate is false and stock basis (lines 1 and 2) is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Disposed of stock in an S corporation (whether or not gain is recognized)"; p. 3, Line 13: "This includes the reduction to basis for the sale or redemption of part of your stock... attach two separate forms."
findings.fix: Add to the gate an input: "For this S corporation, did you or your spouse sell, exchange, give away, or otherwise dispose of any of its stock in 2025, or did the corporation redeem any of your shares?" A yes makes Form 7203 required.

findings.who: A shareholder whose S corporation repaid all or part of a loan they made to it in 2025. They have no loss item and no distribution this year, and their debt basis had been reduced by earlier losses.
findings.why_no: The gate does not test for a loan repayment, so it is false. The loans question, whose yes would end the interview, is never asked, and the gain on repayment (capital for a formal note, ordinary for open account debt) is silently dropped.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Received a loan repayment from an S corporation."; p. 4, Line 34: "Debt evidenced by a formal note will result in capital gain... Any open account debt... will result in ordinary gain and should be reported on Form 4797."
findings.fix: Ask the loans question regardless of the gate, or add to the gate: "For this S corporation, did it repay any money you or your spouse had lent it, in 2025?" A yes makes Form 7203 required and leads to the refusal.

findings.who: Spouses filing jointly who each hold a separate K-1 from the same S corporation. Only one spouse's K-1 shows a loss or a code D distribution.
findings.why_no: If the k1s helper is evaluated per corporation from only one K-1, rather than per K-1 and per shareholder, the other spouse's loss, distribution, or loan facts may not trigger the gate for their own Form 7203.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 2, Name of Shareholder: "If you are married filing jointly and you received a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) for you and your spouse, complete a separate Form 7203 for each spouse."
findings.fix: Evaluate the gate per K-1 (per shareholder spouse), and word each gated question "you" or "your spouse" according to whose K-1 it is.
